# GEO report: quay-store **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points). How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. The cap applies because `robots.txt` blocks Googlebot from the whole site (GEO-009). That cap limits both numbers to 40. Everything here was read from code. The site is small and the code settles every rule. Two things drag the score down: Googlebot is blocked from the whole site, and pages are drawn only in the browser, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript may see empty pages. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot - **Why it matters:** Googlebot is told to stay away from every page, so Google can't read the site at all. This also lifts the score cap. - **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4-5` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 72. GEO-009 and GEO-014 become Clear (+6, 18 ÷ 25), and the cap goes away. ### 2. Put the page content in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** Many crawlers don't run JavaScript. With server rendering turned off, they receive an empty shell. - **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` - **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line, or use `prerender = true` for these static pages. - **Score after this:** 40 on its own, because the cap from item 1 still applies. Together with item 1 it is 84 (21 ÷ 25). ### 3. Add the page language and the missing shop description - **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines which language the site is in. An empty description gives them nothing to show for `/shop`. - **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` - **What the code says:** `` and `` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 40 on its own. After items 1 and 2 it is 92 (23 ÷ 25). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt` is valid | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access you intend | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:4-5`, Googlebot blocked site-wide | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/shop` are blocked for Googlebot by `robots.txt:5` (0 of 2 routes clear) | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Clear | Not run | `/` and `/shop` have absolute canonicals on `quay.example`, which matches the sitemap | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`, site-wide | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid and complete | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`, Product has only `name` (no `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating`) | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt:7` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang are set | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang`. `/shop` has an empty description (`shop/+page.svelte:3`). `/search` has none. | | GEO-016 | Key pages are reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5` has `` links to `/` and `/shop` | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions that conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` on one element (`+layout.svelte:7`), which is a deliberate, scoped choice | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read the layout and all 3 pages: no images, links have text, every page has a title | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found. This is never scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app | ## Other problems found - `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5` is `{@html \`\`}`. It labels the whole "All parts" listing page as a single Product, so the structured data points at the wrong thing. Remove it, or add real product data and put one Product on each product page. ## Worth considering - **Make each part findable:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:9`: `

Bilge pumps, cleats and rope.

`. Each item could have its own page with a price and description, listed in the sitemap, so people have something specific to land on. - **Say the delivery terms in normal text:** `src/routes/+layout.svelte:7`: `
Free delivery over £50.
`. Machines can read it, but it is excluded from snippets. The home page claims "shipped next day" in `src/routes/+page.svelte:3` and gives no delivery details. A visible delivery section would back that claim up. - **Add a viewport tag and a `
` landmark:** `src/app.html:4-8` has `charset` but no `viewport`, and the content sits in a bare `
`. These help phones and screen readers. - **Link onward from the home page:** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7`: `

Marine parts, shipped next day

` is the only content. Nothing tells visitors what is sold or points to product categories. - **Give `/search` a reason to exist for machines:** it is correctly `noindex` (`search/+page.svelte:3`), so no change is needed. Keep it out of the sitemap, as it is now. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Live-only checks:** real status codes, redirects, `X-Robots-Tag` headers and whether the sitemap URLs answer 200 need a live scan. The domain `quay.example` looks like a placeholder, so confirm the real domain. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, since there is no `geo.config.json`. - `https://quay.example` is the intended site origin, because the canonicals, the sitemap and `robots.txt` all use it. - Sampled all 3 routes: `/`, `/shop` and `/search`. `/search` is deliberately `noindex`, so it is excluded from the indexing and canonical checks. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
